newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: WEAK NEW ZEALAND DLR LOOSENS MONETARY CONDITIONS.
newsitem.headline: WEAK NEW ZEALAND DLR LOOSENS MONETARY CONDITIONS.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar fell to a fresh 29-month low on Friday, loosening monetary conditions well below the Reserve Bank's desired levels for the September quarter.

At 3.15 p.m. (0315 GMT), the Monetary Conditions Index (MCI), which measures the mix of the wholesale 90-day bank bill rate and the kiwi dollar's Trade-Weighted Index, fell to 725 -- 100 basis points below the RBNZ's desired level of 825.
"People aren't really too concerned abou it because the perception is that the RBNZ aren't going to do anything about it," said a dealer.
"People are just going to test them now until they say something I guess."
Dealers said the weak Australian unit continued to weigh on the kiwi, which at US$0.6350/60 is at its lowest level since early March, 1995.
"It's probably going to struggle now to get back up through 0.6380. I think we'll have a look at 0.6330 in the next day or two," the dealer said.
The kiwi has fallen eight cents, or 11 percent against the greenback, since November last year.
The kiwi opened Friday's session at 0.6373/80 and at 64.41 on the TWI, while the 90-day rate opened at 8.32 percent.
